title: Forming the band at Nick's in the Village
summary: Nick hears of Sharkey and asks him to put a jazz band in his cellar club; it clicks and earns enough to build a new place.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And he used to talk to Nick a lot about me, see. So Nick found out that I was in New York, and he sent for me, and I went down and talked to him, and he said, I'd like to have you put a band in my place. So I said, I'd be happy to. He says, they never did have jazz here. All we had was piano players and singers, but I think that maybe we put a jazz band in here.
It might create something. It's a little tiny place. I hardly remember.

In other words, it was a cobweb place. Yeah, I heard you there. Down in the cellar. And so I got a band together, George Brunus. George Brunus. First time I heard George in person. Bill Bourgeois, a fella by the name of Turk on the bass, and Bowman. I don't know if you know Bowman, Red Bowman, he played piano.
Yeah, yeah, the pianist. He was from New York, I guess.

Yes, and Johnny Castang. Yeah. And they didn't expect any big things to happen, but it just clicked, Bill. From then on he went into the band business. From then on, in fact, we made him enough money to build the new Knicks.
That place across the street, yeah.
And we played there for about a year or something. That's where he made all his money and he built a new place called Knicks.
